summary: Full published-paper extraction checkpoint with 136 interfaces, exact fixed-determinant and iterated-Frobenius conventions, four coordinated Part II proposals and existing-foundation source routes. It extracts nilpotent reductions, crystalline realizations and periodic flows, geometric p-adic rigidity, unitarity and cohomologically rigid companions. Status remains partial: a concrete nonreduced-family BNR obstruction and other independently unreviewed proof findings, external-source closure and Frobenius/representation normalization gates remain. No Lean implementation, proof closure or confirmed author erratum is claimed.

conventions.C: X is smooth connected projective over C, equipped with a polarization; rank r>0; (E,∇) is stable/irreducible and rigid WITH FIXED torsion determinant (L,∇L). Whenever both Betti/de Rham and Dolbeault moduli are compared, use the vanishing rational Chern-class component. Cohomological rigidity is H¹(End⁰)=0. An arithmetic model is selected and shrunk; quantification over all its closed points does not mean all primes in every model.
conventions.P: k perfect of characteristic prime p, Z/k smooth (projective when asserted), Z' its Frobenius twist, F:Z→Z' relative Frobenius and w:Z'→Z the scheme isomorphism. Pure dimension d gives rank(F_*E)=p^d rank(E). A W₂-lift is data. Nilpotency means tensor iterates vanish; the printed level convention is θ^N=0. Match external p−1/p−2 conventions explicitly.
conventions.W: For finite k, W=W(k), W_n=W/p^n and K=Frac(W). Formal connections are separated and complete. Period f>0 and any extension k'/k are explicit. The paper's F-isocrystal means an F^f-isocrystal for some f; neither f=1 nor an integral Frobenius lattice follows by definition. Relative Fontaine–Laffaille theory is not the absolute point theory of R07.3.
conventions.D: Finite-order determinants are transported under inverse Cartier by L↦L^p. To define the finite permutation, range over 0≤a<ord(L), with p prime to that order. Stable and semistable moduli are not interchangeable for properness. Isolated schemes can be nonreduced.
conventions.Q: Complex rigid connections/variations need not have real or integral structures. Generic-fibre, residual and geometric rigidity of a p-adic representation are distinct assertions. All deformation functors used for the fixed-determinant theorems must retain the determinant. Companions compare local characteristic polynomials using the specified coefficient isomorphism, which need not be continuous.
conventions.G: Items describe mathematical targets and imports. 'Missing' means this checkpoint did not find a matching declaration or stage at the pinned baseline, not a proof of global library absence. A source theorem with a proof gate is not relabeled a conjecture and is not certified proved by this extraction.

items.name: Simpson correspondence in the projective component
items.statement: In C, stable Higgs bundles with vanishing rational Chern classes correspond to irreducible flat connections, compatibly with the torsion determinant. The induced moduli correspondence is real analytic, preserves isolated points and hence gives equality of the finite counts of rigid objects. This is not an equivalence between all Higgs bundles and all connections in positive characteristic.

items.name: Riemann–Hilbert comparison
items.statement: For smooth projective complex X, analytification and horizontal sections identify algebraic integrable connections with complex local systems; the stable fixed-determinant Betti and de Rham moduli are analytically identified. Preserve the topological versus étale fundamental groups and do not assert an algebraic isomorphism of these moduli.

items.name: GL rigidity versus projective rigidity
items.statement: For a finitely generated abstract Γ and irreducible characteristic-zero representation over algebraically closed K, fixed-determinant GL rigidity is equivalent to PGL rigidity. Scalar character twists account for one direction; the reverse requires lifting the µ_r obstruction over the chosen henselian/formal deformation ring. items.statement: For ρ:π₁^top(X)→GL_r(F_q) absolutely irreducible with fixed determinant, the associated continuous representation of the profinite completion is rigid iff its fixed-determinant Betti moduli point is isolated. Prove the bijection on finite Artin-coefficient representations and identify the formal completion. State the PGL counterpart separately as the same proof with projective conjugacy.

items.statement: For a rigid absolutely irreducible projective representation of π₁^top(X) defined over the localized number-field lattice in §5, after a finite Galois extension of the arithmetic model's function field its prime-to-M profinite realization extends to π₁(X_L). Construct the Galois stabilizer and extension data; invariance of a conjugacy class alone is not an arbitrary GL lifting theorem.

The Qp-theory's nilpotent Higgs fields are small; deformations stay in the comparison range used to test rigidity.

items.statement: For a rigid periodic Higgs object, the geometric generic-fibre representation from LSZ corresponds under Faltings to a Frobenius shift σ^m of the original Higgs bundle. Prove this via the direct sum of all f shifts (period one), Faltings's crystalline example and identification of simple summands. Do not assert the shift m is zero or canonical.

Verify separately the residual convention of Definition 5.3 if that stronger assertion is exported.

items.statement: The same geometric representation is rigid with its determinant fixed, via deformation-compatible Faltings comparison and rigidity of the shifted Higgs bundle. Generic-fibre rigidity alone does not prove rigidity of the residual representation; the interface between Definition 5.3 and the proof is an explicit completion gate.

items.name: Good primes: coefficient fields split
items.statement: For the finite collection of rigid rank-r representations, infinitely many primes p satisfy the coefficient-field embedding/splitting requirements, so the rigid W(F_q)-representations and their projectivizations in the stated family descend to Z_p. Apply Cassels to a finite-type subring of C containing all coefficients and relevant normalizations; using a normal closure makes complete splitting explicit. routes.brief: Extend the already-proposed HodgeStructuresPartII, coordinated with PAPER-LANDESMAN-LITT-24, from the parent Hodge structures (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HodgeStructures) to the geometric interfaces in EG20. Import the reviewed/built fibrewise pure, polarized and period-domain algebra; do not assume a complex VHS has an integral lattice. Build projective stable Betti/de Rham/Dolbeault moduli with fixed torsion determinant, Riemann–Hilbert and Simpson on the vanishing-Chern-class component, rigid/cohomologically rigid loci with End⁰ tangent space, nilpotency of rigid Higgs fields, smooth arithmetic models of all isolated points, λ-connections, equivariant rigid Hodge-moduli splitting, Griffiths filtrations and complex variations. The final foundational results are EG20 Lemmas 2.1, 3.1, 4.9 and Propositions 3.3, 4.10, and the equivalence between vanishing graded Higgs field and unitary monodromy. Import generic connection/crystal carriers from CrystallineCohomology:CR.1, moduli foundations from AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry and scheme spreading from SchemeAndStackFoundations. Add the integral-versus-strongly-integral distinction and the rank-one infinite-image unitary example; source-gate the separate EG18, Langer–Simpson SL3 and BKT inputs. The p-curvature nilpotency and Frobenius construction belong to the Cartier/flow successor, while unitarity from zero p-curvature and companion bijections belong to the rigid-arithmetic successor. Keep this foundational Hodge stage independent of those consumers to avoid a dependency cycle.

routes.title: Semisimple algebras, Artin–Wedderburn and module structure, Part II: geometric Azumaya and Morita descent

The needed equivalence concerns sheaf algebras over nonreduced spectral schemes, with descent and annihilator control; neither field Skolem–Noether nor the endoscopic Hitchin roadmap supplies it.
routes.brief: Start from Semisimple algebras and Artin–Wedderburn (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/SemisimpleAlgebras), Mathlib IsAzumaya and Tau Ceti field-level central-simple/Brauer declarations. Extend once to sheaf Azumaya algebras, splitting modules and coherent Morita equivalence over general scheme bases. The foundational theorem is equivalence of modules over End(P) with modules over the base for a finite projective generator P, compatible with annihilators, affine pushforward and the local-free rank calculations used in EG20 Theorem 2.17. Prove strict-henselian splitting, transition invertible bimodules, and descent of the reduced characteristic invariant even on nonreduced parameter schemes. Coordinate geometric Brauer comparison with SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2, already requested by PAPER-CESNAVICIUS-19; it is a supplier, not a duplicate Brauer owner. Import quasi-coherent sheaves and étale descent from SchemeAndStackFoundations/AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry. Export the Cartier one-form connecting map and its functorial/additive Brauer-class interpretation, while the special crystalline D-algebra and its W₂ splitting remain in the Cartier-transform successor. No assertion of unique isomorphisms between arbitrary modules, and no ordinary-henselian splitting without a residue-field condition, is permitted.

routes.title: Crystalline cohomology, Part II: Cartier transforms and periodic rigid connections
routes.reason: CR.1 owns crystals and quasi-nilpotent connection comparison, but its layers do not promise crystalline differential-operator Azumaya theory, inverse Cartier in families or Higgs–de Rham flow. R07.3 owns absolute Fontaine–Laffaille theory; relative filtered connections on a variety are additional.
routes.brief: Extend Crystalline cohomology (CrystallineCohomology), importing CR.1 crystals/connections and CR.2 comparison rather than constructing rival carriers. With HodgeStructuresPartII supplying stable Higgs moduli and nice arithmetic models, build restricted tangent derivations, p-curvature with its Frobenius-semilinearity and horizontality, relative Frobenius, tensor nilpotency, the crystalline D-algebra and its cotangent centre, BMR rank p^(2dim Z), Cartier descent and the W₂-dependent Ogus–Vologodsky equivalence with explicit signs and nilpotency range. Import sheaf Morita descent from SemisimpleAlgebrasPartIIGeometricMorita. Correct the family BNR invariant conditions as in E2/034–035 before the nonreduced deformation proof; locate an explicit R(r,m) support bound and repair E3. Then prove EG20 Theorem 1.4: a rigid stable fixed-torsion-determinant complex connection has a selected arithmetic model with nilpotent p-curvature at every closed point. Build signed inverse Cartier, finite and mixed-characteristic periodic flows, LSZ/SYZ realization and its reduction compatibility; import only the absolute Fontaine–Laffaille input from FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.3. Prove the finite permutation over all determinant powers, lift independence at the level of rigid points, unique filtered lifts, and the finite inverse-limit argument. The second final result is Theorem 1.6: every permitted W(k)-point yields an F^f-isocrystal after finite residue-field extension, with the stronger filtered integral realization specified separately. Develop the Appendix-A scaling/PD action only after repairing the relative Brauer argument E5; retain Corollary A.7's p>2, W₂-liftability and cohomological rigidity hypotheses. This is not a proof of Question A.8 or Simpson motivicity.

routes.title: P-adic differential equations and rigid cohomology, Part II: rigid connections and companions
routes.reason: RD.3 and RD.6 supply geometric coefficients and weights. None of their existing layers states Faltings/LSZ compatibility, rigid p-adic representations, the zero-p-curvature unitarity result or the cohomologically rigid companion bijections. This successor consumes, not repeats, the Cartier-flow construction.
routes.brief: Extend P-adic differential equations and rigid cohomology (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology) from its frame/coefficient and p-adic-weight foundations to arithmetic rigid connections. Import periodic crystalline realizations from CrystallineCohomologyPartIICartierFlows, projective stable Hodge/Betti theory and unitarity criterion from HodgeStructuresPartII, fixed-determinant deformation functors from GlobalGaloisDeformations, and étale fundamental-group specialization from InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups. Build the Faltings small p-adic Simpson input and the LSZ comparison by direct sums of Frobenius shifts, keeping generic, geometric and residual rigidity distinct. Prove EG20 Theorem 5.4 in its verified convention; construct Cassels good points densely in arithmetic opens, projective arithmetic descent and projective period one. Theorem 6.1 concludes UNITARY monodromy from vanishing p-curvature on every closed fibre of a model; finite monodromy needs the extra hypotheses in Propositions 8.1/8.2. For companions, import CR.2 coefficient comparison and RD.6 weights, explicitly source-gate Abe's crystalline shtuka realization and Abe–Esnault p-to-ℓ existence rather than substituting the ℓ-adic GS.6 theorem. Construct local-polynomial companions, finite normalized geometric comparison sets, geometric irreducibility, End⁰-H¹ vanishing by L-functions/purity, determinant-order control and the counting bijection. Final Theorem 7.3 gives p↔ℓ and p↔p companions only for this cohomologically rigid family. Corollary 4.17 gives motivicity only after restriction to a complete-intersection curve and a dense open. The higher-dimensional motivicity problem remains a question. Resolve all source gates and arithmetic-Frobenius normalization before treating the design as closed.

prerequisites.citation: C. Simpson, Higgs bundles and local systems, Publ. Math. IHÉS 75 (1992), 5–95 [Si1]

prerequisites.citation: C. Simpson, The Hodge filtration on nonabelian cohomology, in Algebraic Geometry (Santa Cruz 1995), Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 62, AMS, 1997, 217–281 [Si4]

prerequisites.citation: N. Katz, Algebraic solutions of differential equations (p-curvature and the Hodge filtration), Invent. Math. 18 (1972), 1–118 [Ka2]
prerequisites.why: The Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture that Theorem 1.8 addresses, and Proposition 4.1.2.3, which turns 'unitary with integral monodromy' into finite monodromy in §8.2.

prerequisites.citation: R. Bezrukavnikov, I. Mirković and D. Rumynin, Localization of modules for a semisimple Lie algebra in prime characteristic, Ann. of Math. 167 (2008), 945–991 [BMR]
prerequisites.why: The Azumaya property of the sheaf of crystalline differential operators D_Z over its centre Sym T_{Z′} ⊂ T^*Z′, of rank p^{2 dim Z} — Theorem 2.12 here, on which the whole BNR/Morita mechanism of §2.5 rests.

prerequisites.citation: R. Bezrukavnikov and A. Braverman, Geometric Langlands correspondence for D-modules in prime characteristic: the GL(n) case, Pure Appl. Math. Q. 3 (2007), 153–179 [BB]
prerequisites.why: §4: the Hitchin map for flat connections in characteristic p and the spectral description of D-modules, the setting of §2.5.

prerequisites.citation: Y. Laszlo and C. Pauly, On the Hitchin morphism in positive characteristic, Int. Math. Res. Not. 2001, 129–143 [LP]
prerequisites.why: Proposition 3.2: the characteristic polynomial of the p-curvature defines the morphism χ_dR: M_dR(Z/k,r) → A_{Z′,r} of (2.4), the map every argument in §3 measures deformations against.

prerequisites.citation: D. Xu, Lifting the Cartier transform of Ogus–Vologodsky modulo p^n, Mém. Soc. Math. Fr. 163 (2019), 133 pp. [X]
prerequisites.why: The mod-p^n lift of the Cartier transform, cited beside [LSZ, Theorem 4.1] and [SYZ, §1.2.1] for the functors C_n^{−1} of Theorem 4.5 — the mixed-characteristic half of the Higgs–de Rham flow.

prerequisites.citation: J. W. S. Cassels, An embedding theorem for fields, Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. 14 (1976), 193–198 [Ca]
prerequisites.why: Theorem I: a finitely generated subfield of C embeds in Q_p with prescribed generators going to p-adic units, for infinitely many p. sourceIssues.locator: Published p. 106, the last display of the introduction; compare §7, p. 148
sourceIssues.printed: An irreducible flat connection (E,∇) with torsion determinant L is called cohomologically rigid, if [(E,∇)] is a reduced isolated point of M_dR(X,L,r). This is equivalent to vanishing of  H¹_dR(X,(End(E),∇)) = 0,  and hence explains the nomenclature.
sourceIssues.correction: H¹_dR(X,(End⁰(E),∇)) = 0, the trace-free endomorphisms, as §7 (p. 148) writes it: "Recall that an irreducible connection (E,∇) with determinant L on X over C is called cohomologically rigid if H¹(X,End⁰(E,∇))=0". ("equivalent to vanishing of … = 0" is also one "vanishing" too many.)
sourceIssues.reason: M_dR(X,L,r) is the moduli of connections with the determinant fixed, so its Zariski tangent space at an irreducible point is H¹_dR(X,End⁰(E,∇)) — which is exactly what p. 148 says. In characteristic zero the trace splitting gives End(E) = End⁰(E) ⊕ O_X as flat bundles, so H¹_dR(X,(End(E),∇)) = H¹_dR(X,End⁰(E,∇)) ⊕ H¹_dR(X,(O_X,d)) and the second summand is H¹(X,C), of dimension b₁(X). For every X with b₁(X) > 0 — every curve of positive genus, and every variety the paper is really about — the printed condition therefore holds for no connection at all, and the notion it defines would be empty. Read on the rendered page: the display carries an underlined "End" with no superscript.

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 2.17 and its proof, published pp. 117–119 (especially p. 118, line 8, and p. 119, lines 4–6)
sourceIssues.printed: It is clear that there is at most one such a∈A_{Z′,r}(S) with this property, since a and b are monic polynomials. … By uniqueness of solutions to the equation a^{p^d}=b in Sym^• Ω¹_{Z′×S/S}[λ], we obtain a∈A_{Z′,r}(S) with the required property.
sourceIssues.correction: Both claims fail as soon as S is non-reduced, and so does the essential-image half of the statement of Theorem 2.17. The invariant that is canonical is the one the proof has just built: the characteristic polynomial of the Morita-reduced Higgs sheaf π′_*F, which is independent of the splitting because F is unique up to unique isomorphism. Theorem 2.17 should require of M that this reduced invariant equal a, rather than only that M be supported on Z′_a with π′_*M of characteristic polynomial a^{p^d}; the descent of a should be deduced from that canonicity, not from uniqueness of p^d-th roots.
sourceIssues.reason: Sym^• Ω¹_{Z′×S/S}[λ] is a commutative F_p-algebra, so x ↦ x^{p^d} is a ring endomorphism of it, and it is injective only when the algebra is reduced. Witness for the two printed claims (r=2): let k be a field of characteristic p > 0, Z′ an elliptic curve over k with a nowhere-vanishing ω ∈ H⁰(Z′,Ω¹), and S = Spec k[ε]/(ε²). Then a = λ² + εω² and a₀ = λ² are distinct monic elements of A_{Z′,2}(S) with a^{p} = λ^{2p} + ε^pω^{2p} = λ^{2p} = a₀^{p}, so b = λ^{2p} has two monic degree-2 roots. Witness for the statement (r=3, d=1): take a = λ³ + εω²λ and a₀ = λ³, again with a^p = a₀^p. Since a vanishes on the zero section, Z′ ×_k S ⊂ Z′_a, so the D_{Z′}-module M of the constant family (F^*V,∇_can) with V of rank 3 — whose p-curvature is zero — is scheme-theoretically supported on Z′_a, and π′_*M is locally free of rank 3p with characteristic polynomial λ^{3p} = a^{p}. M therefore satisfies every condition on the right-hand side of Theorem 2.17 for this a, while the connection it corresponds to has Hitchin invariant a₀ ≠ a: the asserted equivalence of groupoids fails. Over reduced S the printed argument is correct and nothing changes. The correspondence is applied over non-reduced bases exactly where it matters — the Artinian deformations in the proof of Proposition 3.5, and the divided-power thickenings of Appendix A — so the repair is needed, but no main theorem depends on the defective half: §3 uses the equivalence C_a supplied by [OV, Corollary 2.9] for an OV-admissible a, and the forward assignment (E,∇) ↦ (χ_dR(E,∇),M) is unaffected.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.5, published p. 127, lines 5–10
sourceIssues.printed: By construction, the family (E_{T_t^{(m−1)}},∇_{T_t^{(m−1)}}) has the property that χ_dR((E_{T_t^{(m−1)}},∇_{T_t^{(m−1)}})) is a morphism T_t^{(m−1)} → A′, and therefore it factors through A′(m−1), but not through A(k−1) for k<m.
sourceIssues.correction: Only the first half is automatic. Truncating an arbitrary deformation at order m−1 can lower the order of its Hitchin invariant, or destroy it; the truncation order has to be chosen so that a non-factoring jet survives, and what the contradiction needs is only that the restriction not factor through A′(D′−1). Since the order required is not bounded by m, the interaction with the standing hypothesis p−1 > R(r,m) has to be re-examined — which is why a uniform bound on the length of a rigid component is the real content here. (A(k−1) is also printed without its prime.)
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample to the inference, with A′ = A¹ = Spec k[u]: take m = 4, T = Spec k[t]/(t⁹) and χ: u ↦ t². Then χ does not factor through A′(3) = Spec k[u]/(u⁴), since χ^*(u⁴) = t⁸ ≠ 0, so T satisfies the hypothesis of the paragraph; but its restriction to T_t^{(3)} = Spec k[t]/(t⁴) has χ^*(u²) = t⁴ = 0, so it factors through A′(1), that is through A′(k−1) with k = 2 < 4 = m, contrary to the printed conclusion. With T = Spec k[t] and χ: u ↦ t^m the restriction to T_t^{(m−1)} is the constant map to 0. The proof of Proposition 3.5 is a proof by contradiction, and this is the step that produces the contradicting Higgs deformation, so the gap is in the load-bearing part of the argument; the conclusion of Proposition 3.5 is not in doubt.

sourceIssues.locator: Definition 5.2, published p. 139, together with Lemma 5.6 and its proof, p. 141
sourceIssues.printed: One denotes by Def_ϱ: Art_F → Sets the functor sending a finite-dimensional commutative local F-algebra A to the set of isomorphism classes of continuous representations ϱ′: Γ→GL(r,A), such that there exists a finite field extension F′/F, an F-morphism A→F′, and an isomorphism (ϱ′)_{F′}≃ϱ_{F′}. We say that ϱ is rigid, if Def_ϱ is corepresented by B∈Art_F. … [Lemma 5.6, proof:] This shows that Def_ϱ̂(F_q) is represented by the formal scheme which is the formal completion of M_B(X/C,det(ϱ),r)⊗_Z F_p at the point [ϱ].
sourceIssues.correction: Def_ϱ must be the fixed-determinant deformation functor — the same convention as everywhere else in the paper — namely the isomorphism classes of continuous ϱ′ with det ϱ′ = det ϱ. Otherwise Definition 5.2 does not define the notion Lemma 5.6 and Theorem 5.4 use.
sourceIssues.reason: As literally defined the functor is the unrestricted one, and it is never corepresented by an Artinian algebra once b₁(X) > 0. Twisting ϱ′ = ϱ⊗χ by a continuous character χ: Γ → 1+m_A is a deformation of ϱ for every A ∈ Art_F, and for p > r distinct characters give non-isomorphic twists (an isomorphism ϱ⊗χ ≅ ϱ forces χ^r = 1 on determinants, and 1+m_A is a p-group). The character functor A ↦ Hom_cont(Γ,1+m_A) is corepresented by the completed group algebra F_q[[Γ^ab ⊗ Z_p]] ≅ F_q[[x_1,…,x_b]] with b = b₁(X), so it acts freely on Def_ϱ and forces the hull of Def_ϱ to have dimension at least b₁(X). For X a curve of genus g ⩾ 1 no absolutely irreducible ϱ would then be rigid, and Lemma 5.6 — whose right-hand side is the completion of the moduli space M_B(X/C,det(ϱ),r) with the determinant fixed — would be false. With the fixed-determinant reading both statements are correct and this is plainly what is meant.

sourceIssues.printed: On the other hand, m^*θ−r^*θ ∈ Ker(H⁰((Z′_a)_p, Ω¹_{(Z′_a)_p/Spec k[t]/(t−1)^p}) → H⁰(Z′_a, Ω¹_{Z′_a})). Thus, m^*θ−r^*θ has support in Z′_p ↪ T^*Z ×_k G′_m, where Z′ ↪ T^*Z′ is the zero-section.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.1, published p. 146, lines 3–5
sourceIssues.printed: Since there are infinitely many prime numbers p such that there exists a good closed point s∈S (Lemma 5.11), we conclude that the Kodaira–Spencer class vanishes everywhere on X_S.
sourceIssues.correction: Apply Lemma 5.11 after inverting a non-zero coefficient of gr(∇_S) — equivalently, after shrinking S — which its own proof allows, since the finitely generated ring R₁ ⊂ C chosen there may be enlarged at will and Cassels's theorem then sends the adjoined inverse to a p-adic unit. Infinitude of residue characteristics on its own does not give the density the deduction needs.
sourceIssues.reason: The good points of Lemma 5.11(c) are closed points of S of pairwise distinct residue characteristics, and such a family need not meet every non-empty open subset of a positive-dimensional arithmetic base: in Spec Z[t] the closed points (p,t), p prime, realise every residue characteristic and all lie in V(t), where the non-zero section t vanishes. The vanishing of a section at all of them therefore does not make it zero. What is true, and is what the proof needs, is this: gr(∇_S) is a section of a coherent sheaf on the integral scheme X_S, so it is non-zero if and only if it is non-zero on the generic fibre; if gr(∇_C) ≠ 0 there is a non-empty open V ⊂ S over which it is non-zero, and a good point inside V contradicts the vanishing established for every good s. The rest of the proof is unaffected: on the reduced fibre X_s the identity gr(∇_s) = ω·id together with nilpotency does force ω = 0.
